articles.title: The root-to-tip revolution! An A-Z of how to eat plants in full – for extra flavour, fibre and savings
articles.description: If you discard the peels, skins, stalks and seeds when consuming fruit and vegetables you are missing out on a lot of value. Here’s what to incorporate into your diet – and what to avoid Do you peel your potatoes, deseed your squash and core your cauliflower? A study by King’s College London, published last month in the International Journal of Food Sciences and Nutrition, found that people who routinely discard peels, skins, stalks and seeds when preparing fruit and vegetables are missing out on a valuable source of dietary fibre. Ten out of the 12 types of produce the researchers analysed had higher levels of fibre in the scraps than in the flesh. Eating these often overlooked parts could help address the global dietary fibre deficit and tackle food waste, they say. Here, experts share their advice on how to cook and eat “root to tip”.
